originality.rationale: The new theorem is the signed first-order total-variation asymptotic, not the previously known Cauchy weak limit or exact density. Llibre–Rondón (2023), Theorem 2(g), and Appis–Llibre (2024), Theorem 4(c), classify relevant global centers. The closest published Cauchy-occupation result provides the exact finite-energy density and weak limiting Cauchy law, but its full theorem/proof/limitations do not supply a first-order signed L1 expansion or the positive Clausen constant. The sharp logarithmic-phase TV law applies to a different cubic polynomial field. The result is a quantitative advance requiring moving-endpoint L1 control, not a reformulation of a prior output.
residual_risks: Unindexed or unpublished equivalent first-order total-variation estimates could exist.
Sharp rate is derived from an exact density already known; publication priority depends on treating a substantive stronger convergence mode and exact constant as an independent mathematical result.
The general 2013 Liénard period article was inspected at abstract level only; its focus is qualitative period monotonicity, not full-time occupation measures.

value.rationale: The leading signed correction is an L1-differentiability theorem for time-sampled periodic-orbit laws, implying an asymptotically sharp, coefficient-universal TV rate with explicit Clausen constant. Unlike previously proved weak Cauchy convergence, it controls all measurable events uniformly, including moving tail events, and all bounded observables. The quantity is a natural and informative exact invariant of this global-center high-energy limit; not merely a finite sample or routine table recomputation.
